posts.subject: Monitor screen blanks for  few seconds
posts.author: levid
posts.message_html:
Lenovo Legion Pro 7 connected to an external screen. Both screens (laptop and external) will go black for a few seconds and return. Happens with two different setups.

  1.  USB-C connection to external monitor and hub
  2. HDMI connection to HDR external monitor

Updated all software and drivers; tried changing power settings.

posts.subject: Re:Monitor screen blanks for a few seconds
posts.author: Sharan2050
posts.message_html:
Both screens going black at once, across two different connection types, usually means the GPU driver is resetting or the system is switching graphics modes. It's unlikely to be a cable, hub, or monitor problem.

Check what Windows logged
Open Event Viewer → Windows Logs → System and look for events at the moments of the blackouts. "Display driver nvlddmkm stopped responding and has successfully recovered" (Event 4101) confirms a GPU driver reset. Messages about a display or power transition point to mode switching instead. This tells you which of the fixes below to focus on.

Most likely fixes, roughly in order

Change the GPU mode. The Legion Pro 7 has a MUX switch. In Legion Space, Vantage, or the BIOS, try Discrete GPU mode instead of Hybrid/Advanced Optimus (or the reverse if you're already on Discrete). Hybrid mode switching is a very common cause of both screens blanking, especially with external monitors. A reboot is required after changing it.

Turn off variable refresh and HDR as a test. Disable G-Sync in the NVIDIA Control Panel and turn off HDR and Auto HDR in Windows Settings → System → Display. Set both screens to a fixed refresh rate. HDR and VRR renegotiation between the monitor and GPU often causes brief blackouts.

Do a clean driver install. Run Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU) in Safe Mode, then install the latest NVIDIA driver from NVIDIA directly. Updating over the old driver can leave bad settings behind. If the problem started after a recent driver update, try the previous version.

Disable Multiplane Overlay (MPO). This is a known cause of brief black flickers on NVIDIA systems with multiple displays. NVIDIA has published a registry fix, and a quick search for "disable MPO NVIDIA registry" will show it.

Turn off hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling in Settings → System → Display → Graphics → Default graphics settings.

Reset any GPU tuning. If you've overclocked or undervolted the GPU or used a Legion performance preset, return everything to stock. Unstable clocks can cause driver resets.

Update the BIOS and EC from Lenovo's support page, since Legion BIOS releases often include display and MUX fixes.

posts.subject: Re:Monitor screen blanks for a few seconds
posts.author: Hassen_Lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello levid,

Welcome to the Lenovo Community, and sorry you're experiencing this issue.

Since the black screen occurs on both the built-in display and an external monitor, and you've already tested two different connection methods (USB-C and HDMI), it sounds less likely to be an issue with a specific monitor or cable.

When both screens go black, does audio continue playing and the system remain responsive, or does it appear the entire system briefly freezes?

Please try the following:

  1. Update both the integrated graphics driver and NVIDIA graphics driver from the Lenovo Support website for your Legion Pro 7, or check for available updates through Lenovo Vantage.

  2. Check in Lenovo Vantage for any BIOS or chipset updates that may be available.

  3. If HDR is enabled on the external display, temporarily disable it and test for a period of time.

  4. If your model supports GPU working modes in Lenovo Vantage, test whether the behavior changes in Hybrid Mode versus dGPU Mode, restarting after each change.

  5. Open Event Viewer and check for any Display, nvlddmkm, or graphics-related warnings/errors around the time the screens go black.

  6. If you're using a dock or hub with the USB-C setup, temporarily connect the monitor directly to the laptop and test again.

The answer to the question above may help determine whether this is a display signal interruption or whether Windows itself is briefly becoming unresponsive.

Best regards,

Hassen_Lenovo
